title: Comfortable towns, ungrateful for their comfort, now empty.
subtitle: When ease turns into arrogance

key.label: Who owns it in the end

then: Addressing the people of Makkah, Allah points to towns that {trap}denied the blessing of ample provision{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says their land became empty; you can see nothing but their dwellings. He compares it to the example of {idea}a township secure and content{/idea} that turned ungrateful.
now: A full fridge, a car that starts, a salary that lands every month. It is easy to stop noticing, then to feel entitled. {trap}Comfort without gratitude is how the slide begins.{/trap}
old: My comfortable life is simply what I have earned.
new: Ease is a blessing to thank Allah for, and it can be taken when it breeds arrogance.
try: Before your next meal, name three blessings in the room and thank Allah for each.

title: No town is destroyed before a messenger reaches it.
subtitle: Allah's justice comes before His punishment
then: Ibn Kathir says this shows {idea}Allah's justice: He destroys no one unjustly{/idea}. The "mother town" is Makkah, and the Prophet ﷺ was sent from it to all people, Arab and non-Arab. He cites the hadith in the Two Sahihs: {idea}"I have been sent to the red and the black."{/idea}
now: You feel like life is ambushing you. But look back: the reminders came first. The friend's advice, the verse in Friday's khutbah. {idea}Allah warns before He holds anyone to account.{/idea} That is a mercy, and an invitation to listen now.
new: Allah always sends a reminder first and only holds the wrongdoers to account.
try: Think of one reminder you have received lately. Act on one small part of it today.

title: Everything you have is decoration for a short life.
subtitle: What lasts versus what shines
then: Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}this world compared to the Hereafter is as if one of you dipped his finger in the sea; let him see what comes back{/idea}. The verse ends by asking those who prefer this world: {trap}will you not use reason?{/trap}
now: You save for months for the new phone. Two years later it is in a drawer, slow and scratched. {idea}Look at what is on your finger, and then at the sea.{/idea} Enjoy what you have, but do not trade the lasting for it.
old: The things I own now are what really matter.
new: What I have is a short enjoyment; what is with Allah is better and lasts.
try: Before your next purchase, pause and give a small amount in charity first.

title: A promise kept, or a few days of luxury?
subtitle: Two lives that only look similar
then: Ibn Kathir explains the comparison: the one who believes in Allah's promise for righteous deeds, {reward}which he will undoubtedly attain{/reward}, against the one who {trap}enjoys a few days in this life{/trap} while denying the meeting with Allah. Mujahid narrated it was revealed about specific Makkans; Ibn Kathir says the meaning is more general.
now: Two colleagues earn the same, drive similar cars, scroll the same apps. One quietly gives, prays, keeps promises. {idea}From outside they look alike. The endings will not be.{/idea}
old: As long as my life looks good, it does not matter what I live for.
new: Two similar-looking lives can lead to very different endings, depending on what I trust.
try: Do one thing today only because Allah promised a reward for it.

title: Where are the partners you used to claim?
subtitle: A question that will be asked one day
then: Ibn Kathir describes this as a rebuke: {trap}where are the gods you worshipped in the world? Can they help you?{/trap} He links it to the verse where people come before Allah {idea}alone, as He created them{/idea}, all they claimed having vanished.
now: You may not bow to statues, but you might lean on things the same way: your boss's approval, your followers, your savings. {idea}Ask what you are treating as your rescuer.{/idea} Then ask whether it will be there when you need it most.
old: Idolatry is about statues, so it has nothing to do with me.
new: Anything I rely on instead of Allah is a partner that will not answer when it matters.
try: Name one thing you rely on more than Allah. Hand that worry to Him in a short dua.

title: The ones who misled you will disown you.
subtitle: When leaders and followers turn on each other
then: Ibn Kathir says these are the devils and those who called people to disbelief. They will {trap}testify against their followers and declare their innocence{/trap}. He cites Ibrahim's words: on the Day of Resurrection {trap}you shall disown each other{/trap}.
now: The friend who said "everyone does it" and talked you into it. The influencer whose advice you followed blindly. {trap}When it goes wrong, they will not stand next to you.{/trap} Choose whose lead you follow with that in mind.
old: The people pushing me toward wrong will share the blame.
new: Those who mislead me will disown me, so I must own my choices now.
try: Think of one voice that pulls you toward wrong. Mute or step back from it this week.

title: They call, and nothing answers. If only they had been guided.
subtitle: A wish that comes too late
then: They will be told to call on their partners to save them, {trap}as they hoped in this world{/trap}. No one answers. Ibn Kathir says when they see the punishment {idea}they will wish they had been among the guided in this world{/idea}.
now: You keep telling yourself you will sort out your prayer after exams, after the wedding, after the promotion. {idea}This verse is the "if only" said too late.{/idea} You still have the chance to say it early.
old: I will take guidance seriously later in life.
new: The wish to have been guided is only useful while I am still alive to act on it.
try: Pick one thing you keep postponing for your faith and do the first small step today.

title: How did you answer the messengers?
subtitle: The second question on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir says the first call is about Tawhid; this one asks {idea}how you dealt with the Messengers sent to you{/idea}. He compares it to the questions in the grave: who is your Lord, who is your Prophet, what is your religion. The believer answers; {trap}the disbeliever says "I do not know"{/trap}.
now: Imagine being asked tonight: how did you respond to the message? Not what you scrolled past, not what you meant to do. {idea}What you actually did with it.{/idea} You are writing that answer this week.
old: Knowing about the Prophet ﷺ is the same as following him.
new: The question will be how I responded to the messengers, not just what I knew.
try: Choose one sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ you know but do not practise, and do it today.

title: Every answer goes blank, and no one can help.
subtitle: No asking around on that Day
then: Mujahid said {trap}the proof will be obscured from them{/trap}, so they cannot ask one another for help by virtue of their blood ties. Ibn Kathir adds: whoever is blind to Allah's signs in this world will be blind in the Hereafter.
now: In the exam hall your mind goes blank, and you cannot lean over to ask your friend. {idea}This is that feeling, but final.{/idea} The only notes you get to bring are the ones you wrote in your life.
old: My family's faith will cover for my own.
new: On that Day no one can whisper me the answer; I need to prepare it now.
try: Spend five quiet minutes today reflecting on what your honest answer would be.

title: But whoever turns back, believes, and does good will succeed.
subtitle: The door still open after the warning
then: After the hard scenes, Allah opens a door: one who repented, believed and did good {reward}will be among the successful{/reward}. Ibn Kathir notes the word "perhaps", when Allah uses it, means {idea}the thing will inevitably come to pass{/idea}, by His grace and mercy.
now: You have read the warnings and feel heavy. You think of the things you have done. {reward}This verse is for you.{/reward} Turn back today, believe, do one good thing. Allah's "perhaps" is a promise.
old: After what I have done, success with Allah is out of reach.
new: Repentance, faith and good deeds lead to success, and Allah's promise of it is sure.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one specific thing, then do one good deed to follow it.

title: He creates what He wills, and He chooses.
subtitle: The choice that is not ours
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah alone {idea}creates and makes decisions{/idea}; no one can dispute with Him or reverse His judgement. What He wills happens and what He does not will does not. He links it to {idea}"It is not for a believer... to have any option"{/idea} once Allah has decreed.
now: You did not choose your parents, your height, the year you were born, the illness that showed up. {idea}Some choices were never yours.{/idea} That can feel like a loss, or a relief: the Wise One chose them.
old: If I did not choose it, it must be a mistake.
new: Allah creates and chooses, and what He chose for me came from His wisdom.
try: Name one thing about your life you did not choose. Say alhamdulillah for it once today.

title: He knows what you hide and what you show.
subtitle: No gap between inside and outside for Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}knows what is hidden in their hearts, just as He knows what they do openly{/idea}. He cites the verse that it is the same whether you conceal speech or declare it, {idea}hidden by night or out by day{/idea}.
now: You smile at the colleague and resent them inside. You give in public, then complain in private. {idea}To Allah there is no backstage.{/idea} That is uncomfortable, and also freeing: you do not have to perform for Him.
old: What I keep inside does not really count.
new: Allah knows my hidden heart exactly as He sees my actions, so I can be honest with Him.
try: Tell Allah one hidden feeling you have not admitted to anyone and ask Him to purify it.

title: His is the praise, first and last, and the decision.
subtitle: Praise in both lives, and the return to Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains: in all that He does, {reward}He is to be praised for His justice and wisdom{/reward}. His decision cannot be put back. Everyone returns to Him on the Day, and {idea}none of their deeds will be concealed{/idea}.
now: You say alhamdulillah after a good meal. Can you say it at the bus stop in the rain, or after the rejection email? {idea}The praise is His in the first life and the last{/idea}, not only in the good moments.
old: I praise Allah when things go my way.
new: All praise belongs to Allah in every situation, because His decisions are just and wise.
try: Say alhamdulillah once today right after something goes wrong.

title: What if the night never ended?
subtitle: Morning light as a gift you never asked for
then: Allah reminds His servants of the night and day, {reward}without which they could not survive{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says continuous night would be harmful, causing {trap}boredom and stress{/trap}. Which god besides Allah could bring the light back?
now: Think of a winter where it is dark when you leave for work and dark when you come home. How heavy that feels. {idea}Every sunrise is something Allah sends{/idea}, not something owed to you.
old: Sunrise is just how nature works.
new: Each morning's light is a mercy only Allah brings.
try: Tomorrow, step outside or open a window at first light and thank Allah for it.

title: And what if the day never stopped?
subtitle: Rest as a gift, not a weakness
then: If the day never ended, Ibn Kathir says, {trap}their bodies would get tired from so much movement and activity{/trap}. Only Allah could bring {reward}a night to rest from your work{/reward}. The verse asks: will you not see?
now: Your laptop is open at midnight. The emails never stop and your phone glows by the bed. {idea}Night is Allah's gift so you can stop.{/idea} Treating rest as laziness is turning down something He made for you.
old: Resting means I am falling behind.
new: Night and rest are mercies from Allah, given so my body can recover.
try: Tonight, put your phone away thirty minutes before sleep and thank Allah for the night.
